postTitle: One Income, No Backup: Planning for a Household of One
topic: One person needs more than half of a couple's budget, because shared bills stay

assumptions.notes: Lesson figures: a couple's budget of €3,000 a month, about €2,100 for one person (about 70%). The split into €1,200 of shared bills and €900 a person is the reel's own illustration of why.

hookVariants.narration: You live alone. Would half a couple's retirement budget cover you?
onscreenLines: Would half a couple's budget cover you?

beats.narration: In this example, shared bills cost one thousand two hundred euros a month.
Other spending is nine hundred euros per person.
Living alone removes one person's nine hundred euro share.
The shared bills stay. That leaves two thousand one hundred euros for one person.

cta.narration: Send this to someone who thinks living alone means half the bills.
cta.subtext: Some bills stay when you live alone

caption.instagram:
You live alone. Would half a couple's budget cover you?

The example: a couple spends €3,000 a month. €1,200 is shared bills, such as rent, heating and internet, and €900 is each person's own spending. Living alone removes one person's €900. The shared bills stay, which leaves €2,100: more than half.

Statisticians use a rule for this. A widely used version, described by the OECD, says one person needs about 70% of a couple's budget for the same standard of living. None of this means a single person needs to be richer; it means the plan runs on its own numbers.
